gap: No result ChatGPT got pairs each pack with the cart controllers and charging ports it is sold for: Allied's RS Big Box kit is listed for modified or lifted carts with controllers up to 450 A, while LiTime caps its 48V 100Ah at 5,000 W in a golf cart (about 98 A at 51.2 V); Allied's stock charger uses a Snap Plug and needs a separate brand-specific harness to charge through the factory Club Car, EZGO or Yamaha port; and Eco Battery says a Club Car needs no OBC bypass when you use its charger.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages and our own result. golfcartshowdown.com (cited) mentions no controller amperage, charger plug type or OBC bypass. Its only fitment claims are that Eco's cart-specific bundles add 'the right charge port and tray' and a note to check Bolt's case shape. golfcartbatterysource.com (cited) gives only general rules: 'A 200-amp limit is enough for a stock cart', 'Some Club Car and EZGO models need an onboard-computer (OBC) bypass', and the cart-voltage classes. It gives no per-product controller limit, plug or harness, and doesn't say which kit avoids the OBC bypass. Our own page (dealectric.com, rank 4) already has LiTime's 5,000 W cap and Vatrer's fit lists, but not Allied's controller limit, Allied's harness pairing or Eco's OBC answer.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's split and gives it a number. LiTime caps its 48V 100Ah at 5,000 W in a golf cart, roughly 98 A at 51.2 V, so it suits a stock cart only. Allied's RS kit is the one listed for a modified or lifted cart with a controller up to 450 A, though that figure comes from a reseller, not Allied. The shopper should read the amp rating on the controller label before choosing between them. If the shopper has a Club Car, Eco's kit with its own charger avoids the OBC bypass. Allied buyers who want to charge through the factory port must order the cart-brand harness ($65) or ask for the plug adapter. On fit lists, our Vatrer Club Car kit covers 48V DS, Precedent, Tempo and Onward.
